Synchronize git hook templates to a target git hooks directory.



Sync installs missing hooks, refreshes hooks whose content drifted from the

template, and repairs hooks that lost their executable bit. Git silently

ignores a hook it cannot execute, so a hook can look installed and still never

run; sync treats that as out of sync.



Use --disable to turn a hook off and --enable to turn it back on. Disabling

renames the hook to <hook>.disabled, which is the standard way to park a git

hook, and sync leaves disabled hooks alone instead of reinstalling them.

  Sync git hooks from tools/git-hooks to .git/hooks
  zqk system sync-git-hooks
  Run dry-run report without making modifications
  zqk system sync-git-hooks --dry-run
  Show which hooks are installed and whether they are enabled
  zqk system sync-git-hooks --list
  Turn off the pre-commit hook
  zqk system sync-git-hooks --disable pre-commit
  Turn the pre-commit hook back on
  zqk system sync-git-hooks --enable pre-commit

Usage:
  zqk system sync-git-hooks [flags]

Flags:
      --disable string   Turn off a hook by name (e.g. pre-commit)
      --dry-run          Report only, exit with error if out of sync
      --enable string    Turn a previously disabled hook back on
      --list             List installed hooks with their enabled or disabled state
      --source string    Source directory containing git hook templates (default "tools/git-hooks")
      --target string    Target directory to install git hooks (default ".git/hooks")

Global Flags:
      --allow-degraded   Allow scheduler-dependent commands to run when scheduler daemon is not running
